There, you will see the weak servant who entrusted his affair to his Master accomplish matters that a whole community of people could not accomplish, and Allah made easy for him what would have been difficult even for the mighty men. And in Allah is the help sought.

{4} Almighty God rebukes His servants for speaking words that have no reality behind them, and God did not make it so as they claimed. That statement from you is a lie and a falsehood, and it entails prohibited matters in the Shari'ah. This is a general rule concerning speaking about anything and reporting the occurrence or existence of what God has not made. However, He singled out these mentioned matters because they were occurring and there was great need to clarify them, so He said:

{"God has not made for any man two hearts within his body."} This does not exist. So beware of saying about anyone that he has two hearts in his body, for you would be lying about God's creation.

{"Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar"} [i.e., that one of you says to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," or "like my mother"]; God has not made them {"your mothers."} Your mother is the one who bore you, and she becomes the woman of greatest sanctity and prohibition for you, whereas your wife is the most lawful of women for you. So how can you liken one of two contradictories to the other? This is impermissible, as God the Exalted said: {"Those of you who make zihar with their wives, they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. Indeed, they utter an evil word and a falsehood."}

{"Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons."} The adopted sons (al-id'iyya') are the child whom a man claims as his own when he is not, or who is ascribed to him because of his adopting him, as was the custom in the Jahiliyyah and the early days of Islam. God the Exalted wanted to nullify and remove this, so He first set forth the ugliness of it and that it is falsehood and lie. Every falsehood and lie is absent from God's Shari'ah and is not to be attributed to the servants of God. God the Exalted says: God has not made those whom you claim as sons, or who are claimed for you, to be your sons, for your sons in reality are those whom you have begotten and who are of you. As for these adopted ones from others, God has not made this equal to that. {"That"}: the saying that you utter about the adopted one, that he is the son of so-and-so who adopted him, or his father is so-and-so. {"is your saying by your mouths"}; that is, a saying that has no reality and no meaning. {"And God says the truth"}; that is, certainty and truthfulness. Therefore He commanded you to follow Him in His saying and His Shari'ah. His saying is true, His Shari'ah is true, and false sayings and deeds are not attributed to Him in any way, nor are they from His guidance, for He guides only to the straight path and the truthful ways. Although that occurs by His will, His will is general to everything that exists, good and evil.

{6} God, exalted is He, informs the believers of a matter by which they come to know the state and rank of the Messenger (ﷺ), so that they may treat him in accordance with that state. He said: {The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves}: the closest thing to a person and the most deserving of him is his own self. The Messenger is therefore more deserving of them than their own selves, because (ﷺ) bestowed upon them such advice, compassion and tenderness that he was the most merciful and kind-hearted of creation. The Messenger of Allah is thus the greatest of all people in bounty upon them, since not an atom's weight of good reached them, nor was an atom's weight of evil averted from them, except by his hands and because of him. Therefore it is obligatory upon them, when the desire of the self or the desire of any person conflicts with the desire of the Messenger, to give precedence to the desire of the Messenger; and that they not oppose the word of the Messenger with the word of anyone, whoever he may be; that they ransom him with their selves, their wealth and their children; that they give his love precedence over the love of all creatures; that they not speak until he speaks, and that they not go ahead of him. This appears to be a preface to what will come in the story of Zayd ibn Harithah, who was previously called Zayd ibn Muhammad, until Allah revealed: {Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men}, and so He severed his lineage and his attribution to him.

He thus informs in this verse that all the believers are children of the Messenger, so no one has superiority over another; and even if the attribution of kinship by calling (da'wah) is severed from some of them, the spiritual (imani) lineage has not been severed from him. The adopted sons who previously inherited by these means, to the exclusion of blood relatives, had their inheritance cut off by this, and God, exalted is He, made it for relatives out of His kindness and wisdom; for if the matter had continued according to the former custom, a great deal of corruption, evil and trickery to deprive relatives of inheritance would have occurred. {Among the believers and the emigrants}: that is, whether the relatives are believers and emigrants or not, for blood relatives take precedence in this. {7–8} He, exalted is He, informs that He took from the prophets in general, and from the Ulul-'Azm (the firm-resolved messengers) in particular—namely these five mentioned—their binding covenant and their solemn, firmly affirmed pledge to uphold the religion of Allah and to strive in His cause. This is a path that the earlier prophets trod, until it was sealed with their master and best, Muhammad (ﷺ), and He commanded the people to follow their example. Allah will question the prophets and their followers about this firm covenant: whether they fulfilled it and were truthful, so that He rewards them with the Gardens of Bliss, or whether they disbelieved, so that He punishes them with painful torment. The groups of Jews who were around Madinah backed them, and they came with great armies and many nations. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) dug a trench around Madinah. This is the habit of the hypocrite in times of hardship and trial: his faith does not hold firm, he looks at the present situation with his deficient reason, and he gives credence to his own assumptions.

{13} And when a faction of them said: among the hypocrites, after they had become fearful and their patience had weakened, they also became among those who discourage others; so they neither endured themselves, nor left people alone from their evil. This faction said: {O people of Yathrib}: they mean: O people of Madinah! They addressed them by the name of the homeland, which indicates the naming in it, signaling that religion and the brotherhood of faith have no weight in their hearts, and that what moved them to this was merely natural cowardice. {O people of Yathrib, there is no station for you}; that is: in the place you have gone out to outside Madinah, for they had encamped beyond the trench and outside Madinah. {So return}: to Madinah. This faction discourages from jihad, and makes clear that they have no strength to fight their enemy, and they order them to abandon the fighting. This faction is the worst and most harmful of the factions. Another faction, below them, was struck by cowardice and fear, and loved to withdraw from the ranks, so they began to offer false excuses. These are the ones of whom Allah said: {And a party of them ask the Prophet for permission, saying: Indeed our houses are exposed}; that is: they are open to danger, and we fear that the enemies will attack them while we are absent from them; so grant us permission that we may return to them and guard them. They were liars in this, {and they are not exposed, though they intend only flight}; that is: their aim is nothing {but flight}. Yet they made this statement a means and an excuse for themselves. These people have little faith, and it has no steadfastness when trials intensify.

{14} {And if the city had been entered upon them}: Madinah, {from its surroundings}; that is: if the disbelievers had entered it from its sides and seized it, (let that not happen). Then these people were asked for {fitnah}; that is: to turn back from their religion and return to the religion of the conquerors and dominators, {they would have given it}; that is: they would have given it readily, {and they would not have delayed in it except briefly}; that is: they have no resolve or firmness in religion, but as soon as the state belongs to the enemies, they give them what they ask and agree with them in their disbelief.

{15} This is their condition, while they had {pledged to Allah before, that they would not turn their backs, and the pledge of Allah will be questioned}: He will question them about that pledge, and find that they broke it; so what then is their assumption about their Lord?

{16} {Say}: to them, rebuking them for their flight and informing them that it will not benefit them at all: {Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing}. Even if you were in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have gone out to their resting places. Means benefit when they are not opposed by the decree and destiny; but when decree and destiny come, every means vanishes and every method a person thinks will save him is nullified. {And then}: when you flee to be saved from death and killing, to enjoy life; {you will not be given enjoyment except briefly}: enjoyment that is not worth your fleeing, your abandoning Allah's command, and your depriving yourselves of everlasting enjoyment in eternal bliss.

{17} Then He made clear that all means avail the servant nothing if Allah wills harm for him, saying: {Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah}; that is: who can prevent you from {Allah if He intends for you harm}; that is: evil, {or intends for you mercy}. Indeed He is the Giver and the Withholder, the Harmful and the Beneficial, who brings no good except Him and repels no evil except Him. {And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector}: one who would take charge of them and bring them benefits, {nor any helper}: one who would help them and repel harms from them. So let them obey the One who alone governs all affairs, whose will prevails and whose decree proceeds, and whom no protector or helper can benefit when His guardianship and support are abandoned.

For this reason He concluded the verse with two names indicating forgiveness, bounty and kindness, saying: {Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful}: Forgiving of the sins of those who transgress against themselves, even if they have multiplied disobedience, when they come with repentance. {Merciful}: toward them, in that He granted them success in repentance, then accepted it from them, and concealed from them what they had committed.

Their multitudes had deceived them, they were pleased with their confederation, and they rejoiced in their numbers and equipment. Then Allah sent upon them a mighty wind, the east wind, which shook their positions, overturned their tents, overturned their cooking pots, and unsettled them, and Allah struck them with terror, so they departed in their rage. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verses 28–29:

{28} When the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) united against him in jealousy (*ghayrah*), and asked him for maintenance and clothing, they requested of him something he could not provide at all times. They remained united in their demands, yet they were insistent in what they wanted. This grieved the Messenger, to the extent that the matter reached the point where he swore off his wives for a month. Allah wished to ease the matter for His Messenger, to raise the rank of his wives, and to remove from them every matter that would diminish their reward. So He commanded His Messenger to give them a choice, and said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment﴾. That is: you have no desire for anything other than it, and you are pleased when it is present and angered when it is absent; so I have no need or want of you while you are in this state. ﴿Then come, I will provide for you﴾: something of what I have of the worldly life, ﴿and release you in a gracious release﴾: that is, I will part from you ﴿without any quarrel or reviling, but with openness of heart and ease of mind, before the matter reaches what is not fitting.

{29} ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode﴾: that is, these are your aim and the ultimate purpose of your seeking. When you attain Allah, His Messenger and Paradise, you will not care about the abundance or scarcity of the world, its ease or its hardship, and you will be content with what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) can afford, and you will not ask of him what is burdensome for him. ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾: He attached the reward to their description of good-doing, because it is the cause that necessitates it, not to their being wives of the Messenger; for merely that does not suffice, and indeed it benefits nothing in the absence of good-doing. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them the choice in this matter, and all of them chose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode; not one of them held back. May Allah be pleased with them all.

In this giving of choice there are many benefits:
Among them: the care for His Messenger and the protectiveness (*ghayrah*) over him, that he should not be in a state where the many worldly demands of his wives burden him.
Among them: the Prophet's (ﷺ) being spared, through this choice, the burden of the rights of wives, and that he remains free in his own self: if he wishes he gives, and if he wishes he withholds, ﴿there is no blame upon the Prophet regarding what Allah has ordained for him﴾.
Among them: the exoneration of him (ﷺ) from what would be the case if among them were one who preferred the world to Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, or who kept company with such a preference.
Among them: the safety of his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, from sin and from exposing themselves to the displeasure of Allah and His Messenger. Through this choice, Allah cut off from them the discontent toward the Messenger that would necessitate his displeasure, which in turn displeases their Lord and necessitates His punishment.
Among them: the manifestation of their elevated rank and high station, and the demonstration of the loftiness of their aspirations, in that Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode were their desire and aim, rather than the world and its trash.
Among them: their readiness, through this choice, for the matter of choosing the best, to attain the highest of the degrees of Paradise, and to be his wives in this world and the next.
Among them: the appearance of the fitting match between him and them; for he is the most perfect of creation, and Allah willed that his wives be perfect, made perfect, good, and made good: ﴿Good women are for good men, and good men are for good women﴾.
Among them: that this choice calls for and necessitates the contentment in which the heart finds rest and the chest is expanded, and it removes from them the greed of covetousness and the lack of contentment that necessitate the heart's anxiety, its agitation, its concern and its sorrow.
Among them: that their choosing this should be a cause for increasing their reward and multiplying it, and that they should attain a rank in which no other woman shares. For this reason He said:

So they were obedient to God and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, and thereby their reward was made known.

{32} God Most High says: {O wives of the Prophet}: an address to all of them. {You are not like any of [other] women, if you fear God}: for by that you surpass all women, and none among women can equal you. So complete your taqwa (God-consciousness) with all its means and aims. For this reason He guided them to cut off the means to what is forbidden, saying: {So do not be soft in speech}; that is, when addressing men, or in a manner that they can hear, so that you become tender in speech and speak with a gentle tone that invites and stirs desire {in whose heart is a disease}; that is, the disease of lustful desire for adultery. Such a person is prepared and waits for the slightest stimulus to move him, because his heart is not sound. For a sound heart has no desire for what God has forbidden, and such a heart is hardly inclined or moved by these causes, owing to its health and freedom from disease. This is unlike the person whose heart is diseased, who cannot bear what a sound person bears and cannot endure what a sound person endures. The slightest cause that arises and calls him to the unlawful, he answers its call and does not resist it. This is evidence that means have the rulings of their ends. Softness of speech and gentleness in it is, in origin, permissible, but since it becomes a means to the forbidden, it is prohibited. For this reason, a woman, when addressing men, should not soften her speech to them.

When He forbade them to be soft in speech, it might be assumed that they were commanded to speak harshly. He removed this assumption by saying: {and speak a known word}; that is, not harsh and not rough, just as it is not soft and submissive. Reflect on how He said {do not be soft in speech} and did not say "do not be gentle in speech." This is because what is forbidden is the soft speech in which a woman submits to a man and humbles herself before him, and the one who is submissive is one who is coveted. This differs from one who speaks gently without any submissiveness, indeed perhaps with dignity and dominance over the opponent, for such a person is not coveted by his adversary. For this reason God praised His Messenger for gentleness, saying: {It was by a mercy from God that you were gentle with them}, and He said to Moses and Aaron: {Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed. And speak to him a gentle word that perhaps he may remember or fear}.

His saying {so that one in whose heart is a disease may be moved to desire}, together with His command to guard the chastity and His praise of those who guard their private parts, male and female, and His prohibition of approaching adultery, indicates that when a servant finds this state within himself, that he is delighted by performing the forbidden when he sees or hears the speech of one he desires, and finds that the motives of his desire have turned toward the unlawful, he should know that this is a disease. He should strive to weaken this disease, extinguish evil thoughts, struggle against his soul to keep it safe from this dangerous disease, and ask God for protection and success. This is part of guarding the chastity that he is commanded to observe.

{33} {And stay in your houses}; that is, remain in them, for that is safer and better protects you. {And do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance}; that is, do not go out often adorned or perfumed, as was the custom of the people of the former ignorance, who had neither knowledge nor religion. All of this is a prevention of evil and its causes.

Having commanded them to taqwa in general, and specifically named some particulars of taqwa because women have need of them, He likewise commanded them to obedience, especially prayer and zakat, which everyone needs and depends upon. They are the greatest acts of worship and the most noble acts of obedience. In prayer there is sincerity toward the One worshipped, and in zakat there is kindness toward the servants.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verse 35:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the reward of the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) and their punishment should they fail to comply, and that none among women is like them, He mentioned the rest of the women apart from them. Since the ruling for them and for men is one, He made the ruling common to both, saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾. This refers to the outward legislated duties (shara'i', the apparent rulings of the religion) when they are upheld. ﴿And the believing men and believing women﴾. This refers to inward matters, the beliefs of the heart and its deeds. ﴿And the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women﴾; that is, those who obey Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And the truthful men and truthful women﴾ in their speech and their actions. ﴿And the patient men and patient women﴾ in the face of hardships and calamities. ﴿And the humble men and humble women﴾ in all their conditions, especially in their worship and above all in their prayers. ﴿And the charitable men and charitable women﴾, in obligatory (fard) and voluntary (nafl) giving. ﴿And the fasting men and fasting women﴾, which includes obligatory and voluntary fasting. ﴿And the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard their chastity﴾, against adultery (zina) and its preliminaries. ﴿And the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember Allah often﴾; that is, at most times, especially at the times of the fixed daily litanies (awrad), such as morning and evening, and after the obligatory prayers. ﴿Allah has prepared for them﴾; that is, for those described with these beautiful attributes and noble virtues, which comprise beliefs, deeds of the heart, deeds of the limbs, and utterances of the tongue, beneficial acts that reach others and those that remain limited to oneself, and the doing of good and the abandoning of evil. Whoever upholds these has upheld the whole religion, outward and inward, through Islam, faith and excellence (ihsan). So He rewards them for their deeds with forgiveness of their sins, because good deeds remove bad deeds. ﴿And a great reward﴾, whose true measure none can know except the One who bestows it, a reward such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. We ask Allah to make us among them.

{36} That is: it is not fitting, nor becoming, for one who has attained faith to do anything but hasten to seek the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, flee from the displeasure of Allah and His Messenger, comply with their command, and avoid what they forbid. Thus it is not fitting for any believing man or believing woman, {when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter}: among the matters, and have made it binding and obligatory, {that they should have any choice about their affair}; that is, whether they should do it or not? Rather, the believing man and woman should know that the Messenger has more right over them than their own selves; so they should not let some of their own desires become a barrier between them and the command of Allah and His Messenger. {And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error}; that is, manifest. For he has abandoned the straight path which leads to the honour of Allah and taken other paths that lead to painful punishment. He first mentioned the cause that necessitates not opposing the command of Allah and His Messenger, which is faith, and then mentioned the deterrent from that, which is the warning of error, indicating punishment and chastisement.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verse 37:

{37} The occasion of the revelation of these verses was that God, exalted is He, willed to legislate a general ruling for the believers: that adopted children (al-ad'iya', sing. da'i) do not have the status of real sons in every respect, and that it is not sinful for one who adopted them to marry their wives. This was one of the customary matters that would hardly be removed except by a great event. So He willed that this legislation be made by His Messenger in both word and deed. When God wills a matter, He makes a cause for it. Zayd ibn Harithah was called Zayd ibn Muhammad, for the Prophet (ﷺ) had adopted him, so he came to be called by that name, until the verse ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾ was revealed, and he was then called Zayd ibn Harithah. Zaynab bint Jahsh, the daughter of the paternal aunt of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), was married to him. It had occurred to the heart of the Messenger that if Zayd divorced her, he would marry her. God decreed that there should be between her and Zayd what required that Zayd ibn Harithah came asking the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission to separate from her. God said: ﴿And [remember] when you said to the one on whom God had bestowed favor﴾, that is, with Islam, ﴿and you had bestowed favor upon﴾ by manumission, guidance and instruction, when he came to you consulting you about separating from her, ﴿you said, "Keep your wife for yourself"﴾, that is, do not separate from her, and be patient with what has come to you from her, ﴿and fear God﴾ in your affairs generally and in the matter of your wife particularly, for fear of God urges patience and commands it. ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which God is to disclose﴾: what he concealed was that if Zayd divorced her, he (ﷺ) would marry her. ﴿And you feared the people﴾ regarding not disclosing what was in yourself. ﴿And God has more right that you fear Him﴾, for His fear brings every good and prevents every evil. ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her﴾, that is, his soul became content, he lost his desire for her and separated from her, ﴿We married her to you﴾. We did this for a great benefit, namely: ﴿so that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾, since they saw you marry the wife of Zayd ibn Harithah, who had previously been attributed to you. Since the statement ﴿so that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons﴾ is general in all circumstances, and since among circumstances there were some in which that was not permitted, namely before he had finished his need of her, it was restricted by the phrase ﴿when they have no longer any need of them, and the command of God is ever performed﴾, that is, it must occur, with no hindrance or obstacle to it.

Among the benefits in these verses containing this story:

First: praise of Zayd ibn Harithah, and this is in two respects. One: God named him in the Qur'an, and He did not name any of the Companions by name other than him. Two: God informed that He had bestowed favor upon him, that is, the favor of Islam and faith, and this is a testimony from God that he was a Muslim believer outwardly and inwardly; otherwise there would be no basis for singling him out with the favor, except that the intended favor is a special favor.

Second: the freed slave is in the favor of the one who freed him.

Third: the permissibility of marrying the wife of the adopted son, as it explicitly states.

Fourth: practical instruction is more eloquent than verbal instruction, especially when it is accompanied by speech, for that is light upon light.

Fifth: the love that is in the heart of a servant for someone other than his wife, his female slave, and his unmarriageable relatives, if it is not accompanied by a prohibited matter, the servant does not sin for it. Even if this is accompanied by his wish that, were her husband to divorce her, he would marry her, without striving to bring about a separation between them or causing it by any means whatsoever, because God informed that the Messenger (ﷺ) concealed that within himself.

Sixth: the Messenger (ﷺ) conveyed the clear message, and left nothing of what was revealed to him unconveyed, even this matter in which he was rebuked. This shows that he is the Messenger of God, that he says only what is revealed to him, and that he does not seek to magnify himself.

Seventh: the one who is consulted is trustworthy. It is obligatory upon him, when consulted about any matter, to advise what he knows to be best for the one consulting, and to give precedence to the consultant's interest over his own desire and aim, even if he has a personal stake.

Eighth: among sound opinion for one consulted about separating from a wife is that he be told to keep her as long as the situation can be made right, for that is better than separation.

Ninth: a servant must give precedence to the fear of God over the fear of people, and that He is more deserving of it and more fitting.

Tenth: the virtue of Zaynab, may God be pleased with her, Mother of the Believers, in that God Himself arranged her marriage to His Messenger (ﷺ) without a proposal or witnesses. For this reason she used to boast of it over the wives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying: "Your families married you off, but God married me from above the seven heavens."

Eleventh: a woman who is married may not be wed, nor may efforts be made toward it or its causes, until her husband has finished his need of her, and he does not finish his need of her until her waiting period has ended, because before the end of her waiting period she is still under his marital bond, or within his right in which he has an interest in her, even if in some respects.

Thus the people of uprightness found the way clear, walked behind this leader, recognized through him good and evil and the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness, and were illumined by him to know their Worshipped One, recognizing Him through His praiseworthy attributes, His sound actions, and His rightly guided judgments.

{49} God, exalted is He, informs the believers that when they marry believing women and then divorce them before they have touched them, then there is no waiting period (ʿiddah) for them that their husbands are owed. He commands them to provide for them in this state with something of the goods of this world that will console their hearts for the separation, and to part from them in a good manner, without quarrelling, abuse, demands, or anything else of that sort.

From this verse it is deduced that divorce occurs only after marriage. So if a man divorces a woman before marrying her, or makes her divorce conditional upon marrying her, it does not take effect, because of His saying: ﴿When you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾. He made divorce come after marriage, which shows that before that it has no place. And if divorce, which is a complete separation and a complete prohibition, does not take effect before marriage, then the lesser prohibition, such as zihar (the pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening a wife to one's mother), or ila' (oath of abstention from sexual relations), or the like, is all the more fitting and worthy of not taking effect before marriage, as is the more sound of the two opinions of the scholars.

And it indicates the permissibility of divorce, since God related it concerning the believers in a manner in which He did not blame them for it, nor reproached them, with the verse being introduced by addressing the believers.

And it indicates its permissibility before consummation, as He said in another verse: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾.

And that a woman divorced before consummation has no waiting period, rather, once she is divorced, she may marry immediately where there is no impediment.

And that a woman who has been consummated has a waiting period. As for whether what is meant by "consummation" (dukhul) and "touching" (masis) is sexual intercourse (wat'), which is the agreed position, or whether it also includes seclusion (khalwah) even if no intercourse took place, as the Rightly-Guided Caliphs ruled, and this is the sound view: whenever a man enters upon her and has intercourse with her, or does not, if he is alone with her, the waiting period becomes obligatory for her.

And that a woman divorced before touching is to be provided for according to the means of the wealthy man and according to the means of the poor man. But this applies when no dowry (mahr) has been specified for her; if a specified dowry was set for her, then when he divorces her before consummation, half the dowry falls due, and that suffices in place of the provision (mut'ah).

And that whoever separates from his wife, whether before or after consummation, should make the separation a good one, in which each of them speaks well of the other, and not an ugly one; for there is much evil that follows from each of them disparaging the other.

And that the waiting period is a right of the husband, because of His saying: ﴿you have no waiting period for them to count﴾. Its implication shows that if he divorces her after consummation, he has a waiting period due from her.

And that separation by death requires a waiting period in all cases, because of His saying: ﴿then you divorce them...﴾ the verse.

And that all other separated wives, other than the non-consummated, whether by death or by life, have a waiting period owed by them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verse 50:

{50} Almighty Allah says, bestowing a favour upon His Messenger by making lawful for him what He made lawful, both what he shares with the believers and what is specific to him and exclusive to him: {O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments (ujur)}; i.e., you have given them their dowries (mahr) as wives. This is among the matters shared between him and the believers, for the believers likewise are permitted to marry those women to whom they have given their bridal payments. {And} likewise We have made lawful for you {what your right hands possess}; i.e., the female slaves whom you own, {of what Allah has returned to you as spoils (fa'a)}: from the booty of the disbelievers, their slaves, and free women, whether or not they have husbands among them. This too is shared. Likewise, among what is shared is His saying: {and the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts}: this includes paternal and maternal uncles and aunts, both close and distant. This is a restriction of the lawful women, and from its implication it is understood that other relatives are not lawful, as was mentioned in Surah an-Nisa'; for it is not permitted to marry from the female relatives anyone other than these four categories. Also excluded are all descendants and all ascendants in the direct line, and the descendants of father and mother, even if they are far removed, and the descendants of those above them in the direct line of his loins; for these are not permitted.

His saying: {who emigrated with you} is a condition for the lawfulness of these women for the Messenger, as is the correct of the two opinions in the interpretation of this verse. As for other than him, peace and blessings be upon him, it is known that this is a condition for validity only. {And} We have made lawful for you {a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet}: merely by her giving herself, {if the Prophet wishes to take her in marriage}; i.e., this is subject to his will and desire, {exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the believers}; meaning: the permission concerning the woman who gives herself is specific to you. As for the believers, it is not lawful for them to marry a woman merely because she has given herself to them. {We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and what their right hands possess}; i.e., We have already known what is incumbent upon the believers, and what is lawful and unlawful for them of wives and of what their right hands possess, and We have informed them of that and explained its obligations. Whatever in this verse differs from that is specific to you, because Allah made it an address to the Messenger alone with His saying: {O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you...} to the end of the verse. His saying: {exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the believers}: We have permitted you, O Prophet, what We did not permit them, and We have extended to you what We did not extend to others; {so that there will be no discomfort upon you}: and this is from the increased care of Allah Most High for His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. {And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful}; i.e., He has never ceased to be characterised by forgiveness and mercy, and He bestows upon His servants of His forgiveness, mercy, generosity and kindness what His wisdom requires, and the causes of it are found among them.

This is also part of Allah's expansion of favour upon His Messenger and His mercy towards him, in that He permitted him to leave off dividing his time equally among his wives as an obligation. If he does so, it is a voluntary act of kindness (tabarru') on his part. Nevertheless, the Prophet (ﷺ) would strive to divide his time among them in everything, and he would say: "O Allah! This is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what I do not possess." Here Allah says: ﴿You may postpone whom you wish of them﴾; that is, you may delay whichever of your wives you wish, not taking her to yourself and not spending the night with her. ﴿And you may take to yourself whom you wish﴾; that is, you may embrace her and spend the night with her. ﴿And whomever you seek [to take] from those you had set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾; and despite all this, this matter is not obligatory. The meaning is that the choice is entirely in your hand in all of this. Many of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: this applies specifically to the women who gave themselves to him, that he may postpone whom he wills and take to himself whom he wills; that is, if he wills, he accepts the woman who has given herself to him, and if he wills, he does not accept her. And Allah knows best.

Then He explained the wisdom behind this, saying: ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve and be content with what you give them, all of them﴾; that is, the expansion granted to you, the matter being left to your discretion and in your hand, and what comes from you to them being a voluntary act on your part, is more likely to comfort their eyes and prevent them from grieving, and to make them content with what you give them, all of them, because they know that you have neglected no obligation and have not failed in any binding right. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾; that is, what arises in them when fulfilling obligatory and recommended rights, and when rights conflict. Therefore, O Messenger of Allah, the expansion was legislated for you so that the hearts of your wives may be at ease. ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing, Forbearing﴾; that is, of vast knowledge and abundant forbearance. From His knowledge is that He legislated for you what is most beneficial for your affairs and most increasing in your rewards, and from His forbearance is that He did not punish you for what proceeded from you and for what your hearts persisted in of evil.

This is a thanks from God, who has always been Most Appreciative (Shakur), to the wives of His Messenger, may Allah be pleased with them, in that they chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. He showed them mercy and restricted His Messenger to them, so He said: {No women are lawful for you after this}: that is, your present wives. {Nor is it [lawful] for you to exchange them for other wives}; that is, nor is it lawful for you to divorce some of them and take a replacement for her. Through this, they were secured against co-wives and against divorce, because Allah had decreed that they are his wives in this world and the Hereafter, and there will be no separation between him and them. {Even if their beauty impressed you}; that is, the beauty of others, so they are not lawful for you. {Except what your right hand possesses}; that is, the slave-girls (suriyy, concubines); this is permissible for you, because enslaved women, in their potential to cause dislike among wives, are not in the same position as wives in harming them. {And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful}; that is, Observer of affairs, Knower of what they will come to, and Sustainer of their management in the most perfect order and the finest arrangement.

{53} God, exalted is He, commands His believing servants to observe proper conduct with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when entering his houses. He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal﴾; that is, do not enter them without permission to enter for the sake of food. Likewise, do not be ﴿waiting for its preparation﴾; that is, waiting and lingering until it is ready, or until there is room for you after finishing it. The meaning is: you may not enter the houses of the Prophet except under two conditions: that you are permitted to enter, and that your sitting be limited to the measure of need. For this reason He said: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation﴾; that is, before the meal and after it.

Then He explained the wisdom and benefit of the prohibition, saying: ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet﴾; that is, your waiting beyond the need causes him hardship and distress, your detaining him from the affairs of his household and his occupations in it. ﴿So he would be shy of you﴾ — that he would tell you, "Leave!" — as is the customary practice, that people, especially the generous among them, are shy to put people out of their dwellings. ﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾: the legislated command, even if it is imagined that abandoning it would be a matter of courtesy and modesty. Indeed, resolve in its entirety lies in following the legislated command, and in being certain that whatever contradicts it is not of courtesy in any way. God, exalted is He, is not shy to command you with what is good for you and gentle toward His Messenger, whatever the circumstance.

This is their conduct regarding entering his houses. As for their conduct with him concerning his wives: when they have need of something, either it is necessary or it is not. If it is not necessary, there is no need for it, and courtesy lies in abandoning it. If it is needed, such as asking them for an item or other household utensils or the like, then they are to be asked ﴿from behind a partition﴾; that is, there should be between you and them a screen that shields from sight, since there is no need for seeing them. Thus looking at them is prohibited in every case, and their speech is subject to the detail that God mentioned. Then He mentioned the wisdom of that in His saying: ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, because it is further from suspicion. The more a person distances himself from the causes that call to evil, the safer it is for him and the purer for his heart. Therefore, among the legislated matters whose many details God has explained is that all means of evil, its causes and its precursors, are prohibited, and that it is legislated to keep away from them by every means.

Then He said a comprehensive word and a general principle: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God﴾ — O assembly of believers; that is, it is not proper or fitting for you, but rather the most abominable thing — ﴿nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾. This is among the things that harm him, for the Prophet (ﷺ) has a station of honor, exaltation and dignity, and marrying his wives after him violates this station. Also, they are his wives in this world and the Hereafter, and the marital bond remains after his death; therefore it is not lawful for any of his community to marry his wives after him. ﴿Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾. This community has indeed complied with this command and avoided what God forbade in it, and to God belong praise and thanks.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verse 55:

{55} When He mentioned that they should not be asked for a utensil except from behind a screen, and the wording was general for everyone, it was necessary to make an exception from it for those mentioned who are mahrams (those with whom marriage is forbidden), and that ﴿there is no blame upon them﴾ in not veiling before them. He did not mention the paternal uncles and maternal uncles in it, because if they do not veil from those who are their paternal aunts and maternal aunts, the children of their brothers and sisters, despite their elevated status over them, then not veiling before their paternal uncle and maternal uncle is all the more fitting. Also, the explicit text of the other verse that mentions the paternal uncle and maternal uncle takes precedence over what is understood from this verse. And His saying: ﴿nor their women﴾, meaning: there is no blame upon them in not veiling before their women, i.e., those who are of their kind in religion, so this excludes the women of the disbelievers. It is also possible that the intended meaning is the category of women, for a woman does not veil before a woman. ﴿Nor what their right hands possess﴾: as long as the slave is entirely in her possession. And when He lifted the blame from these people, He stipulated for this and for other than it the obligation of fearing Allah, and that there be no legally prohibited matter in that, so He said: ﴿and fear Allah﴾, meaning: practice His taqwa (God-consciousness) in all circumstances. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾: He witnesses the deeds of the servants, outward and inward, hears their statements, and sees their movements; then He recompenses them for that with the most complete and perfect recompense.

{56} This contains an alert to the perfection of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the elevation of his rank, the loftiness of his station with Allah and with His creation, and the raising of his remembrance. "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet" — that is, Allah praises him among the angels and in the Exalted Assembly, out of His love for him, and the angels brought near to Him praise him, supplicate for him, and humble themselves before Him. "O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace" — in emulation of Allah and His angels, as a recompense for some of his rights over you, as a perfecting of your faith, as a glorification of him (ﷺ), as love and honor, as an increase in your good deeds, and as an expiation of your bad deeds. The best forms of sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings be upon him) are those which he taught to his Companions: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious." This command to send blessings and peace upon him is prescribed at all times, and many of the scholars made it obligatory in the prayer.

{57–58}

When Allah, exalted is He, commanded the glorification of His Messenger (ﷺ) and invoking blessings and peace upon him, He then forbade harming him and threatened those who do so. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger﴾. This includes every harm, whether spoken or done, such as cursing and insulting, or belittling him, his religion, or anything that brings harm back to him. ﴿Allah has cursed them in this world﴾, meaning He has removed them far away and expelled them. Among the curse upon them in this world is that the killing of one who insults and harms the Messenger becomes obligatory. ﴿And in the Hereafter, and He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾, as recompense for their harming him, they are to be harmed with a painful punishment. The harming of the Messenger is therefore not like the harming of anyone else, because a servant does not believe in Allah until he believes in His Messenger (ﷺ). He has a standing of honour, which is among the necessary requirements of faith (al-iman), that requires that he not be treated like anyone else. Although harming the believers is also grave and its sin is great, Allah said concerning it: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women for what they have not earned﴾, meaning, without any offence on their part that would justify the harm. ﴿Then they have borne a slander﴾, meaning upon their backs, ﴿and a clear sin﴾, because they harmed them without cause and violated a sanctity that Allah commanded to be respected. For this reason, insulting an individual believer is cause for discretionary punishment (ta'zir, a punishment not fixed by the Law) in proportion to his condition and the elevation of his rank. Thus the discretionary punishment for one who insults the Companions is more severe, and the punishment for one who insults the scholars and people of religion is greater than for others.

{59} This is the verse known as the verse of hijab (veiling). God commanded His Prophet to instruct women in general, and to begin with his wives and daughters, because they are more emphatically bound by it than others, and because one who commands others should begin with his own family before anyone else, as God says: ﴿O you who believe, save yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾. ﴿That they should draw their jalabib (outer garments, sing. jilbab) over themselves﴾: these are the garments worn over the clothes, such as a wrap, a veil, a mantle, and the like. That is, they should cover their faces and chests with them. Then He mentioned the wisdom behind this, saying: ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed﴾. This indicates that harm would occur if they did not veil, because when they do not veil, one may think they are not chaste, so that the one in whose heart is a disease approaches them and harms them. And they may be belittled and thought to be slave women, so that one who intends evil treats them with contempt. Thus veiling cuts off the desires of those who covet them. ﴿And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He forgave you what has passed and showed you mercy by making the rulings clear to you and explaining the lawful and the unlawful. This, then, closes the door from the side of the women.

{60–61} As for the side of the people of evil, He threatened them by His saying: ﴿If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease and the agitators in the city do not cease﴾. "Disease" means the disease of doubt or of desire. "The agitators" (al-murjifun) are those who spread fear and terror among the enemies, who talk about their large numbers and strength and the weakness of the Muslims. He did not mention the act they should cease from, so that it would encompass everything their souls inspire in them, whisper to them, and call them to of evil: insinuating insults against Islam and its people, spreading false alarm about the Muslims, weakening their strength, and pursuing the believing women with evil and immorality, and other sins committed by people like these. ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾; that is, We will command you to punish and fight them and give you authority over them. Then, when We do that, they will have no power against you, and they will have no strength or means of resistance. For this reason He said: ﴿Then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little﴾; that is, they will not remain your neighbors in the city except for a little, by your killing them or banishing them. This is evidence for banishing the people of evil whose presence among the Muslims causes harm, for that is more decisive in cutting off evil and keeping it farther away. They will be ﴿cursed; wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a [thorough] killing﴾; that is, they will be driven away wherever they are found, having no security and no settled place, fearing that they will be killed, imprisoned, or punished.

{62} ﴿[This is] the way of God with those who have passed on before﴾: that whoever persists in disobedience and dares to cause harm and does not desist from it, he will be punished with a severe punishment. ﴿And you will not find in the way of God any change﴾; that is, any alteration. Rather, the sunnah (way) and custom of God flow in accordance with the causes that necessitate their effects.

{63} That is: people ask you about the Hour, hastening towards it, and some of them to deny its occurrence and to challenge the one who told of it. {Say}, to them: {The knowledge of it is only with Allah}; that is, none knows it but Allah. So neither I nor anyone else has knowledge of it. And despite this, do not be slow about it: {And what would make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.}

{64–66} The mere coming of the Hour, whether near or far, carries no outcome or benefit in itself. The outcome, loss, gain, wretchedness and happiness lie in whether the servant deserves punishment or deserves reward. So I will tell you about these and describe for you those who deserve them. He described those who deserve punishment and described the punishment, because the described attribute applies to these deniers of the Hour. He said: {Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers}; that is, those for whom disbelief has become their habit and their way, disbelieving in Allah, His messengers, and what they brought from Allah. So He has removed them from His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, and that is sufficient as a punishment. {And has prepared for them a blaze}; that is, a fire kindled and blazing within their bodies, with the torment reaching their hearts. They will abide in this severe torment, never leaving it, and it will not be lightened for them for a moment. {And they will not find for themselves} {any ally} to give them what they asked for, {nor any helper} to repel the punishment from them. Rather, the Most High, the All-Helper, has forsaken them, and the torment of the Blaze has encompassed them and reached them to a great extent. That is: Allah showed them his innocence, while he (peace and blessings be upon him) is not the object of accusation or harm, for he was honored in the sight of Allah, brought near to Him, among the chosen of the Messengers and the sincere servants of Allah. His virtues did not restrain them from harming him and confronting him with what he disliked. So, O believers, beware of imitating them in that. The harm alluded to here is the saying of the Children of Israel about Musa, when they saw the intensity of his modesty and his covering himself from them: "He is only prevented from that because he is *adar*," that is, large-testicled, and this became well known among them. So Allah willed to clear him of them. He once bathed and placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment, so Musa (peace be upon him) hastened after it. He passed by the assemblies of the Children of Israel, and they saw him, the most beautiful of Allah's creation, and what they had accused him of was removed from him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 33, verse 70–71:

{70} Allah, exalted is He, commands the believers to be mindful of Him (taqwa) in all their states, in private and in public. He singles out from among these [states] and recommends "qawl sadid" (upright, sound speech), which is speech that conforms to the truth or comes close to it when certainty cannot be attained. This includes recitation, remembrance (dhikr), commanding what is good, forbidding what is evil, seeking knowledge and teaching it, being eager to reach the correct position in matters of knowledge, and following every path and using every means that leads to that. Among upright speech is gentleness and kindness of speech in addressing people, and speech that contains sincere advice and guidance toward what is most beneficial.

{71} Then he mentioned what follows from His taqwa and from speaking upright speech, saying: {He will amend for you your deeds}; that is, that will be a cause of their being made sound and a path to their acceptance, because by employing taqwa deeds are accepted, as Allah, exalted is He, said: {Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous} [5:27]. A person is guided thereby to righteous action, and Allah also amends deeds by preserving them from what corrupts them and preserving their reward and multiplying it. Just as neglecting taqwa and upright speech is a cause of the corruption of deeds, their non-acceptance, and their failure to produce their effects. {And will forgive you} also {your sins}, which are the cause of your ruin. So taqwa sets affairs in order and averts every harm. For this reason He said: {And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment} [33:71].

{72} Almighty God magnifies the status of the trust (amanah) that God entrusted to the responsible human beings (mukallafun). It consists of carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, whether in private and in secret or in public. He, may He be exalted, presented it to the great creations, the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, as an option (takhyir) and not as an obligation (tahtim). If you (fem.) undertake it and fulfill it as it should be, then you will receive the reward, and if you do not undertake it and do not fulfill it, then you will receive the punishment. ﴿But they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾. That is: they feared that they would not be able to do what they had taken on, not out of disobedience to their Lord or disinterest in His reward. God presented it to the human being on that stated condition, and he accepted it and bore it, despite his wrongdoing and ignorance, and bore this heavy burden.

{73} Mankind is divided, according to whether they uphold it or not, into three categories: hypocrites [who showed that they] upheld it outwardly but not inwardly, polytheists who abandoned it both outwardly and inwardly, and believers who upheld it both outwardly and inwardly. God mentioned the actions of these three categories and what they will receive of reward and punishment, saying: ﴿That God may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, and that God may turn in mercy toward the believing men and the believing women. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So to Him, may He be exalted, belongs all praise, for He concluded this verse with these two noble names, which indicate the completeness of God's forgiveness, the vastness of His mercy, and the generality of His generosity, even though those who are judged are many, of whom some did not deserve forgiveness and mercy because of their hypocrisy and polytheism.

The tafsir of Surah al-Ahzab is complete, by the praise and help of God.
